taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-02, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 31374.7 | 20.07 | 20.07
2 | 7559.9 | 12.79 | 32.86
3 | 3573.3 | 1.62 | 34.48
4 | 313.2 | 38.90 | 73.38
5 | 53.6 | 0.41 | 73.79
6 | 22.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as Q-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-02, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-02, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model at T-02 shows six layers with resistivity decreasing monotonically with depth: 31,374.7 Ω·m (0–20.07 m), 7,559.9 Ω·m (20.07–32.86 m), 3,573.3 Ω·m (32.86–34.48 m), 313.2 Ω·m (34.48–73.38 m), 53.6 Ω·m (73.38–73.79 m), and 22.8 Ω·m (basal layer, undefined thickness).

Applying the curve-type convention to each triplet of consecutive layers:
- Layers 1-2-3: r1>r2>r3 → Q
- Layers 2-3-4: r1>r2>r3 → Q
- Layers 3-4-5: r1>r2>r3 → Q
- Layers 4-5-6: r1>r2>r3 → Q

All four triplets yield Q, consistent with a continuously decreasing resistivity profile. The resulting curve type is QQQQ, simplified to Q, matching the on-file classification. No discrepancy is noted; the site's electrical layering is consistent with the recorded Q-type designation.

{"curve_type_stated": "Q", "label_issue_flagged": false}
